title: Find K Closest Elements
description:
Given a sorted integer array `arr` (in non-decreasing order) and two integers `k` and `x`, return the `k` closest integers to `x` in the array. The result must also be sorted in non-decreasing order.

An integer `a` is closer to `x` than an integer `b` if:
- `|a - x| < |b - x|`, or
- `|a - x| == |b - x|` and `a < b`.
constraints: arr is sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Because arr is sorted, the k closest elements always form a contiguous subarray arr[left .. left + k - 1].
Binary search the starting index left in [0, arr.length - k].

Compare the signed distances x - arr[mid] and arr[mid + k] - x (not abs!) so that duplicates and ties are both handled correctly: if x - arr[mid] > arr[mid + k] - x, shift right (left = mid + 1), otherwise right = mid.

examples.explanation: Distances to 3 are [2, 1, 0, 1, 2]. Between 1 and 5 (both distance 2), 1 is preferred since 1 < 5, yielding [1, 2, 3, 4].
Since x = -1 is smaller than all elements, the first 4 elements [1, 2, 3, 4] are the closest.
Distances to 3 are [2, 2, 1, 0, 1, 2]. Among the values at distance 2 (1, 1, 5), the smaller value 1 wins, giving [1, 2, 3, 4].
